Why should you avoid `!!`, and what do y.why: To see whether you treat null safety as a design tool or just silence the compiler.
Why should you avoid `!!`, and what do y.mistake: Saying `!!` is fine because you know the value isn't null, without handling the day that stops being true.
Why should you avoid `!!`, and what do y.followUp: When is `requireNotNull` better than an early return?

What does `inline` do, and when shouldn'.why: To check that you know what the compiler generates, not only the keyword.
What does `inline` do, and when shouldn'.mistake: Claiming `inline` makes any function faster. Without lambda parameters the gain is usually negligible.
What does `inline` do, and when shouldn'.code:
inline fun <reified T> List<Any>.firstOfType(): T? =
    firstOrNull { it is T } as T?

val text = listOf(1, "two", 3).firstOfType<String>()

Can a data class be inherited?.why: A quick check that you know what a data class generates and where its limits are.
Can a data class be inherited?.mistake: Saying a data class can't extend anything. It can't be `open`, but it can have a superclass or interfaces.
Can a data class be inherited?.followUp: How would you model a closed set of UI states instead?

How does `by lazy` work?.why: It shows whether you understand delegation and thread safety behind a one-line keyword.
How does `by lazy` work?.mistake: Using `lazy` for a value tied to a view or Activity in a longer-lived object, so it goes stale or leaks.

If you pass a Kotlin `List` to Java, can.why: To test whether you know that Kotlin's guarantees can end at the Java boundary.
If you pass a Kotlin `List` to Java, can.mistake: Believing a read-only `List` is immutable. It's only a read-only view.
If you pass a Kotlin `List` to Java, can.followUp: How would you stop Java code from changing the list?

What is a higher-order function, and why.why: To confirm you're comfortable with functions as values, which most Kotlin APIs rely on.
What is a higher-order function, and why.mistake: Only saying lambdas are shorter, without mentioning function types or the cost of allocation.
What is a higher-order function, and why.followUp: When does passing a lambda allocate an object?

What is a lambda with a receiver, and wh.why: Receivers power the DSLs you use daily, so this separates using them from understanding them.
What is a lambda with a receiver, and wh.followUp: How would you design a small DSL with a receiver?

How can a lambda leak an Activity?.why: Interviewers want to see that you connect language features to Android memory leaks.
How can a lambda leak an Activity?.mistake: Blaming lambdas themselves. The leak comes from who keeps the reference, and for how long.
How can a lambda leak an Activity?.followUp: How would you find that leak?

What does `@JvmOverloads` do?.why: To see whether you've worked in a mixed Java and Kotlin codebase.
What does `@JvmOverloads` do?.mistake: Thinking Java callers can use Kotlin default arguments directly.

What are guard conditions in `when`?.why: To check whether you keep up with recent Kotlin releases.
What are guard conditions in `when`?.mistake: Putting a guard on a `when` that has no subject, where it isn't allowed.
What are guard conditions in `when`?.followUp: Which Kotlin version made guard conditions stable?

What is a companion object, and how is i.why: It catches people who translate Java habits straight into Kotlin.
What is a companion object, and how is i.mistake: Saying companion members are true static methods. Without `@JvmStatic`, Java calls them through `Companion`.
What is a companion object, and how is i.followUp: When would you use a top-level function instead?

How do you choose between `let`, `run`,.why: Scope functions are everywhere, and choosing well shows you care about readability.
How do you choose between `let`, `run`,.mistake: Nesting several of them until nobody can tell what `this` or `it` refers to.
How do you choose between `let`, `run`,.followUp: Which one would you use to build and configure an `Intent`?

What is the difference between a sealed.why: To see whether you can model state so that invalid cases can't happen.
What is the difference between a sealed.mistake: Using an enum plus nullable fields for data that only some states have.
What is the difference between a sealed.followUp: When would you still pick an enum?
What is the difference between a sealed.code:
enum class Direction { North, South }          // fixed instances

sealed interface Result {                      // each case has its own data
    data class Success(val items: List<String>) : Result
    data class Failure(val error: Throwable) : Result
    data object Loading : Result
}

Explain `out` and `in` in Kotlin generic.why: Variance shows whether you can design generic APIs, not just consume them.
Explain `out` and `in` in Kotlin generic.mistake: Memorising "out is output" without explaining which assignments become safe.

When would you use a sequence instead of.why: It tests whether you pick collection tools for a reason rather than by habit.
When would you use a sequence instead of.mistake: Switching to sequences everywhere and expecting a speed-up on small lists.
When would you use a sequence instead of.followUp: How can a sequence be slower than a list?
